activation.claim: This file specifies required future capture; it does not attest that capture exists or is complete.
required_before_p1t: the dedicated ai-vps-controlled-harness single-writer delivery service is installed and continuously healthy
the exact pre-C1 machine participant, executable, channel, filesystem, process, network, environment, secret, and control-input boundary is frozen
Mac, humans, stock Codex and Claude, the local relay, tmux, agent-sync, and general interactive VPS sessions are proved unable to deliver bytes or control inputs into the harness
one immutable content store, retention horizon, and authentication policy are frozen
the controlled-harness signing public key and key identifier are frozen
a destructive-write, truncation, restart, offline-gap, sequence-conflict, and unexpected-ingress acceptance test passes on the controlled harness
a public target-blind readiness receipt binds service, isolation policy, participant boundary, key, content-store, and acceptance-test digests
the experimenter upstream abstention identities and machine-detectable conflict-exclusion rule are frozen
currently_unset: immutable content-store locator and retention attestation
experimenter upstream abstention and conflict identity binding
activation.transition_rule: A target-blind pre-P1 protocol commit may set executable true only after every required readiness artifact exists. P1T may not precede that commit.

origin.meaning: Who or what produced or controls the delivered bytes.

exposure.meaning: Whether an authenticated delivery path to a frozen experimental participant is proved.

orthogonality: Every evidence unit receives exactly one origin and exactly one exposure class.
No origin value implies an exposure value.
Copied or generated bytes inherit neither origin nor exposure from their container.
Tool origin is not sufficient for MACHINE_REGISTRY_CONTACT.
Authenticated-upstream origin is not sufficient for IMMUTABLE_SOURCE_CUSTODY after rendering.

capture.delivery_definition: Before C1, bytes count as delivered only when they are returned to or consumed by a frozen machine participant, executable, tool consumer, or generated-artifact consumer inside ai-vps-controlled-harness. Public existence or delivery to a proved nonparticipant with zero harness ingress is not experimental delivery.

host_journals.content_rule: Every delivered byte stream is copied to the immutable content store before or atomically with delivery. Truncation, replacement, deletion, and abandoned partial writes receive signed records.
host_journals.chain_rule: The controlled harness uses a strictly monotonic sequence and binds the exact preceding receipt; restarts continue the chain and service-epoch identity is recorded.
host_journals.offline_rule: Benchmark delivery is forbidden while the controlled-harness service is unhealthy. Work performed during an unproved interval invalidates the protocol.

participant_endpoint_capture.rule: Every pre-C1 machine-participant ingress and egress crosses the controlled broker and is durably stored before consumption. Filesystem watchers and periodic endpoint scans are reconciliation only and cannot cure an ingress or journal gap.

required_properties: versioning or write-once retention through the fixed horizon and audit period
no raw semantic bytes in public Actions logs or artifacts

pre_c1_participants: P1-frozen identity, grouping, classification, provenance, quota, and replay executables
P1-frozen broker, custody, checkpoint, and bounded-publication executables
pre_c1_nonparticipants: stock Codex and Claude sessions on every host
participant_isolation.nonparticipant_rule: A listed nonparticipant is outside the benchmark only while frozen controls prove zero read, write, process-memory, socket, credential, environment, network, filesystem, model-context, and control-input ingress into the harness.
participant_isolation.coexistence_rule: A general process may coexist on the physical VPS without becoming a participant only if it cannot read or write harness roots, sockets, credentials, process memory, control requests, or output channels.
participant_isolation.possible_ingress_rule: Any possible unregistered ingress into a frozen participant is PROTOCOL_INVALID even if no later exact alias hit is found.
participant_isolation.post_c1_rule: Only after C1 may fresh isolated arm and independent-verification processes or model endpoints receive target semantics; they receive no inherited session, memory, cache, prior arm result, or shared model context.

upstream_nonintervention.operator_abstention: Frozen experimenter identities must not author, edit, review, request changes to, lobby for, or otherwise influence a future-cohort formal-conjectures cluster during P1T..U2.

required_sources.complete_when: Git object, ancestry, ref-source, and tree receipts authenticate the frozen interval; any bytes rendered beyond the bounded machine lane also have a signed delivery-journal record.

Each explicit controlled-harness root is authenticated, the protocol checkout is read-only, and every byte consumed by a machine participant is present in the signed harness journal and immutable content store.
The frozen controlled-harness signing key verifies one unbroken sequence from P1T through cutoff, every referenced blob exists, and all frozen machine endpoints reconcile to the chain.
An authenticated inventory proves every journal-referenced object exists with exact bytes and frozen retention; the locator, authentication, and retention fields are non-null before P1T.

Every owned-platform byte stream crossing a frozen machine delivery endpoint is captured before consumption or publication and reconciles with signed harness receipts; global platform state is not claimed complete.
The pre-invocation declaration, producer receipt, output object, and signed delivery receipt agree; an undeclared participant ingress invalidates the protocol.

explicit_non_sources.reason: Global public availability is not experimental delivery. Any bytes crossing into a frozen machine participant must be captured by the controlled-harness journal; possible unrecorded ingress invalidates the protocol.

Recursive archival of every Actions log is not the exposure boundary. Only bytes consumed or authored by a frozen machine participant enter the harness journal, and target-bearing hosted-runner execution is forbidden unless that runner is first added to the frozen participant boundary.

Storage outside an explicit harness root is not exposure when zero ingress is proved. Reading it into, or using it to control, a frozen participant is an unregistered channel and invalidates the protocol.

Humans and Mac applications are pre-C1 nonparticipants only under proved zero ingress into the controlled harness. Their independent receipt of public target semantics creates no evidence unit; any possible influence on harness inputs or control is protocol-invalid.

These processes and channels are not captured as participants and may coexist only under proved filesystem, socket, process, credential, environment, network, and control-input noninterference with ai-vps-controlled-harness.

forbidden_omissions: A delivered byte stream may not be omitted because another source appears to duplicate it.
A delivered byte stream may not be omitted because it is believed not to contain a future identity.
An identity-only output may not be omitted after consumption by a frozen machine participant.
Deleted, overwritten, expired, truncated, or inaccessible delivered evidence creates a coverage gap unless an earlier signed content-addressed capture proves the exact bytes.
A frozen machine participant may not use an unregistered host, browser, chat, tool, repository, model endpoint, or generated-output channel during the interval.
Delivery to a nonparticipant may be ignored only when zero ingress or control influence into every frozen participant is proved.
UNKNOWN may not be used to downgrade a missing or possible unregistered participant ingress; that condition is PROTOCOL_INVALID.
Endpoint inventories, Git mirrors, API snapshots, and best-effort sync cannot cure a missing signed journal interval.
